ltv_ruling.ruling: The hazard-based LTV ($7,899.96) is computed as ARPU / monthly hazard = $64.76 / 0.008198 = $7,899.96, which ALGEBRAICALLY implies an expected customer lifetime of 1/0.008198 = 122.0 months (~10.2 years). But tenure in this dataset is right-censored at 72 months (~6 years) and the OBSERVED mean tenure is only 32.4 months -- no customer in the data has ever been observed to reach 122 months. The hazard-based figure is a single-snapshot cross-sectional hazard rate (aggregate customer-months churned / total customer-months observed), and treating it as a constant, indefinitely-repeatable monthly risk for a customer who has ALREADY survived to any given tenure is a survivorship-bias error: customers who reach high tenure in a cross-section are disproportionately the ones for whom month-to-month contracts have already converted to loyalty (churn hazard actually DECREASES with tenure per the Phase 3 cohort/hazard analysis -- see reports/figures/ts_hazard_by_tenure.png), so extrapolating the population-average hazard forward forever massively overstates revenue that will never actually be collected. VERDICT: hazard-based LTV ($7,899.96) is NOT used for campaign ROI. The tenure-based empirical LTV ($2,283.30) is grounded in revenue actually observed to have been collected (not extrapolated), so it is the safer anchor -- though it itself is a lower bound (it mixes complete lifetimes from churned customers with the still-ongoing, not-yet-fully-collected revenue of active customers, so true LTV for an average customer is somewhat higher than $2,283.30, just nowhere near $7,899.96).
ltv_ruling.chosen_value_of_a_save_methodology: Rather than use either full-lifetime LTV figure directly in the EV arithmetic below (both have the biases explained above, and a full-lifetime payoff assumption is unusually optimistic for a monthly retention-campaign ROI decision), this evaluation uses a bounded, standard retention-economics framing: the value of a 'save' is the revenue protected over a stated decision horizon, not the customer's entire remaining lifetime. PRIMARY assumption: 12 months of Month-to-month ARPU ($66.40/mo x 12 = $796.80) -- Month-to-month is used because these are the customers a churn model realistically targets (42.71% churn rate vs 2.83% for Two-year, per Phase 1). This $796.80 figure is well below the tenure-based LTV anchor ($2,283.30), so it is conservative relative to even the safer of the two LTV numbers. A sensitivity range using the tenure-based LTV as an upper alternative is also reported.

assumptions.value_of_save_upper_methodology: tenure-based empirical LTV (conservative anchor, not hazard-based)
